abstract: The paper wasp Polistes dominula (Christ, 1791) is one of the most widespread vespid species in Europe and has become invasive in temperate regions on other continents. In Central Europe its mitochondrial genomes fall into two distinct haplotype groups with overlapping distribution. Whether these groups are reproductively isolated, and thus two bona fide species, is an open question. We sampled P. dominula in southern Germany and the Netherlands, where both haplotypes occur syntopically. We found that individuals with different mitochondrial haplotypes exhibit fixed differences at more than 18,000 nuclear loci and have haplotype-specific cuticular hydrocarbon profiles. They also differ subtly but consistently in wing and body shape, and in Wolbachia prevalence and strain identity. Polistes dominula is thus a complex of two biological species. However, among more than 850 wasps, twelve had ambiguous characters, three of them showing signs of hybridisation. Both reference genomes published as P. dominula belong to Polistes pectoralis (rev. stat.). Our new assembly is therefore the first reference genome of P. dominula sensu stricto. The remarkable variation in ecological, behavioural, and phenotypic traits attributed to P. dominula may reflect differences between the two species.
